This paper proposes Ranging-Assisted Phase Difference of Arrival (RA-PDoA), a scalable BLE localization architecture combining one active anchor performing a standard two-way CS exchange with multiple passive receive-only anchors observing the same transmissions. A channel-recovery framework is derived that enables passive anchors to reconstruct a channel response suitable for super-resolution delay estimation, allowing multipath-robust ranging without participating in a two-way exchange. Coarse arrival-time information is further used to bound the position estimate and reject inconsistent range solutions. A comprehensive evaluation characterizes the impact of multipath propagation, body shadowing, synchronization requirements, oscillator impairments, anchor placement, and deployment inaccuracies, thereby quantifying the practical infrastructure requirements for scalable BLE localization. Simulation results in modeled indoor environments show that RA-PDoA reduces the 90th-percentile localization error from 175.3 cm to 95.5 cm under body shadowing while maintaining an airtime requirement independent of the number of anchors. The results demonstrate that a single active ranging link enables scalable and multipath-robust BLE Channel Sounding localization.

papers.title: Consensus-Constrained Dual-Federated Optimization with Client-Side Dynamic Weighting for Distributed Android Device Threat Defense
papers.summary: Smartphones, smart-home hubs, and wearables are increasingly exposed to sophisticated Android malware, while centralized threat-detection pipelines raise privacy and scalability concerns. Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without collecting raw client data, but partial participation and variation in local model quality can destabilize global optimization. In this article, we propose DW-FedADMM, a federated optimization framework that combines primal-dual coordination with performance-dependent client-side weighting. The dynamic coefficient modulates each participating client's local state before the augmented-Lagrangian update, while the dual variables regulate disagreement between local and global model states. We evaluate DW-FedADMM on three Android malware benchmarks, namely Drebin, Malgenome, and TUANDROMD, with 5, 10, and 15 clients holding IID data shards, partial client participation, and communication budgets of 5 and 10 rounds. Each configuration is repeated with ten random seeds. DW-FedADMM obtains the highest seed-averaged accuracy on Drebin (97.64% +/- 0.20%) and the best mean accuracy in 9 of the 18 dataset-client-round configurations, including 7 of the 9 configurations with a 10-round budget. Pooled over all configurations, it reaches 95.42% accuracy, 94.62% F1-score, 96.06% precision, and 99.45% AUC, compared with 95.32%, 94.51%, 95.56%, and 99.41% for FedADMM, while also giving the lowest mean false-positive rate and the smallest client update norm among the six compared methods. Both primal-dual methods are well ahead of the averaging- and proximal-based baselines on Malgenome and TUANDROMD, where the latter often remain at the majority-class solution when clients are fragmented. The gain of dynamic weighting over FedADMM is most pronounced on Drebin and with the longer communication budget, where it also reduces the variation across seeds.

papers.title: Atik: A Shared-Mesh Transformer Accelerator for RISC-V
papers.summary: Transformer inference repeatedly invokes dense matrix multiplication and attention, including its data-dependent softmax normalization. We present Atik, an open-source RoCC accelerator for RocketChip that executes matrix multiplication and dense attention through one shared fixed-point MAC mesh. Atik accepts and returns BF16 tensors, uses a streaming online-softmax schedule that never materializes the full score matrix, and is invoked through a small descriptor-based ABI. We evaluate three meshes cycle-by-cycle on FireSim and report standalone Sky130 physical-design area. Across 137 logged FireSim test records, all tests pass their benchmark tolerance with zero reported output mismatches. Relative to the same scalar Rocket BF16 reference, the 8x8 configuration reaches 31.5x peak matmul speedup and 225.8x peak attention speedup. Hybrid projections for the single-layer workload-derived C models, using directly measured accelerator-kernel cycles, give aggregate speedups of 44.2x, 77.1x, and 32.3x for ViT, TinyBERT, and GPT-2 prefill, respectively; these are not full-model hardware replays.

papers.title: Beyond Feasibility: Efficient and Robust On-Device Localization with UWB Concurrent Transmissions
papers.summary: Concurrent transmissions (CTX) enable an ultra-wideband (UWB) tag to range to, or self-localize from, multiple nodes with a single frame reception, significantly improving update rate and energy efficiency compared to traditional approaches. Prior work demonstrated the concept feasibility via prototypes whose real-world applicability is however hindered by many limitations, notably including their inability to directly execute on UWB tags and to cope with interfering UWB signals. We address these limitations in two ways. First, we redesign the core CTX techniques to enable a fast and efficient execution on resource-constrained MCUs without sacrificing accuracy. Second, we leverage the new features in the IEEE 802.15.4z standard to achieve robustness to interference from other UWB devices and enable tags to dynamically select which anchors to use, two crucial and unexplored capabilities in CTX-based systems. We quantitatively evaluate our approach experimentally in two real-world testbeds with different characteristics. We first analyze our new techniques individually, offering an in-depth discussion of design choices and performance trade-offs. Then, we embed all our techniques into a CTX-based system enabling a tag to self-localize entirely on-device, unlocking gains up to 44% in runtime and 85% in energy efficiency compared to traditional approaches.

papers.title: TPIC: Energy-Conserving Space Plasma Simulations on GPU Supercomputers
papers.summary: Artificial heating and numerical damping affect particle energization in kinetic space plasma simulations, even when the numerical scheme remains stable. Implicit and semi implicit energy conserving Particle-in-Cell (PIC) methods eliminate these errors in the discrete energy balance while relaxing explicit stability constraints. We present TPIC, a massively parallel implementation of the Energy Conserving Semi-Implicit Method (ECSIM) for GPU supercomputers. We extend the exact energy conservation in the ECSIM formulation to closed domains with conducting boundaries by deriving and canceling a spurious term in the discrete Poynting flux theorem. TPIC executes the complete particle and field cycle on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, combining matrix-engine acceleration with asynchronous communication and computation. We validate TPIC in a variety of electrostatic and electrodynamic test cases relevant for space plasma physics applications, including quasineutral plasma expansion, two-stream instability, Whistler waves, Weibel instability, Whistler turbulence, and three-dimensional magnetic reconnection with conducting walls and 12.3 billion particles. We show that in all scenarios, TPIC agrees with the corresponding analytical theory or reference numerical results, and preserves the total system energy to machine precision. On 4,096 AMD GPUs, TPIC advances 1.9 trillion particles with 96.8\% weak scaling efficiency.

papers.title: Breaking the Privacy Promise: Gradient Inversion Attacks on Federated Low-Rank Adapted Vision Transformers
papers.summary: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) has been increasingly adopted to fine-tune pretrained models with low computational cost and is therefore also preferred in the federated learning paradigm to reduce computational and communication overhead. In this work, we investigate the sparsely explored problem of the risk of private data leakage in LoRA-adapted Vision Transformers (ViTs), where low-rank updates weaken the gradient signal available to a server with access to individual client updates. We show that quality of reconstruction is limited by two coupled ambiguities: reduced information in LoRA gradients and missing spatial cues from frozen positional embeddings. To address this, we propose a spatially anchored generative inversion framework that incorporates server-prescribed trainable positional embeddings into ViT blocks during fine-tuning at clients. The resulting positional gradients act as layer-wise spatial anchors, providing additional positional cues, while the generative prior keeps reconstructions on a realistic image manifold, reducing duplicate-data and patch-permutation artifacts, {which produce similar gradients as those produced when the target client images are used}. Adding our proposed spatial anchoring to GIAS improves PSNR by 10.14 dB, SSIM by 0.45, and LPIPS by 0.098 on CIFAR-10, as well as PSNR gains of 7.83 and 11.74 dB on high-resolution CelebA and CARS datasets, respectively, in the FedSGD setting. Such gains in reconstructed image quality metrics are also maintained at higher batch sizes and in FedAvg settings. These results indicate that LoRA-based PEFT does not, by itself, prevent data leakage in FL, and carefully incorporated positional embeddings can help in exposing private information.

papers.title: A Cross-Domain TARA-to-NAC Rule Mapping Methodology: From Automotive OEM Networks to Energy Storage Systems
papers.summary: Threat analysis and risk assessment under ISO/SAE 21434 ends with cybersecurity goals, but existing methods give little structured guidance for turning those goals into enforceable network access control rules. Compliance standards such as IEC 62443, ISO/SAE 21434, and ISO/IEC 27001 are usually applied as parallel efforts rather than as one enforcement architecture. This paper presents a six-step methodology that maps cybersecurity goals from a threat analysis and risk assessment to network access control rules, each placed at a named enforcement point and traceable to the threat records behind it. It also presents a unified compliance framework that treats IEC 62443 and ISO/IEC 27001 as a fixed substrate and domain-specific regulation as an interchangeable overlay. The methodology is applied to an automotive original equipment manufacturer plant network, addressing multi-tier supplier authorization and legacy operational technology devices, and then to utility-scale battery energy storage, where North American Electric Reliability Corporation Critical Infrastructure Protection standards and ISO/IEC 27019 replace the automotive-specific standard while the substrate stays constant. In the automotive example, 37 threat entries and 24 cybersecurity goals yield 23 rules covering 11 of the 13 in-scope goals; the energy example yields six rules. Three derived rules have no equivalent in the cited standards. Both examples are desk-based: the methodology is applied to them, not tested on them. The result is a reusable pattern for translating risk assessment into enforcement across critical infrastructure sectors, with empirical validation left as future work.

papers.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
papers.summary: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. However, quantum algorithms can only be evaluated by classical computers on restricted or small instances. Here we demonstrate automated discovery of quantum programs beyond these regimes including order-of-magnitude improvements on scientific applications. To achieve this, we build a quantum program library in the Lean theorem prover in which large language model agents synthesize novel programs against formal problem specifications and verify their correctness and cost. Agent teams collaborate, sharing results and knowledge through wikis and discussing ideas at organized conferences. Our results improve on prior baselines for parallel search (up to 1.4x), quantum arithmetic (290x), and simulations relevant to fusion, photochemistry and drug-metabolism by 11x, 8x and 2.5x respectively. Combining human and artificial intelligence at scale, under the rigor of mathematical proof, lets researchers design algorithms that today's classical and quantum computers cannot test, shortening the path to practical quantum computation.

papers.title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
papers.summary: The key-value (KV) cache dominates memory capacity and bandwidth in long-context LLM serving. While 4-bit microscaling formats (NVFP4, MXFP4) shrink the cache and run attention on FP4 Tensor Cores, a fundamental gap remains between algorithmic quantization and system-aware acceleration: existing FP4 KV systems use vanilla quantization that causes severe accuracy drops, whereas accuracy-oriented 4-bit algorithms rely on vector codebooks whose lookup overhead degrades decoding throughput. We present BitDecoding-FP4, an algorithm--system co-design for accurate and efficient native FP4 KV decoding. We mitigate three error sources: Dual-Residual Query Quantization splits queries into two FP4 tensors, cutting query logit error from 60% to 1%; Underflow-Aware Probability Scaling prevents E4M3 scales from rounding long-context probabilities to zero; and Outlier-Aware Key Quantization combines static smoothing, Hadamard rotation, and scale search to suppress key outliers under token-wise scaling. At the system level, we remove the softmax bottleneck via transposed softmax with fused probability quantization and stacked query MMA on paged KV caches. Across dense and MoE models with GQA and MLA, BitDecoding-FP4 stays within 0.5 points of BF16 KV accuracy with NVFP4 (1 point with MXFP4), and tracks BF16 KV in RL training rollouts. In end-to-end serving on NVIDIA B300 with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, it delivers 2.4-3.0$\times$ higher peak serving throughput than BF16 KV. The implementation is available at https://github.com/OpenBitSys/BitDecoding-FP4.

papers.title: Ensemble Methodology for Reference-Free Confidence Estimation in LLM-based Code Summarization
papers.summary: This paper describes an approach and use case to estimate the correctness of LLM-generated COBOL summaries without access to human-authored references. The core intuition is that inter-model agreement on semantics is informative about truth, and that an LLM-as-judge can provide higher-fidelity pairwise assessments than traditional string- or embedding-based metrics. We operationalise this intuition with (i) controlled summary generation from diverse models; (ii) a LLM evaluator that compares pairs of summaries and emits structured judgments; and (iii) a calibrated aggregation rule that combines supportive evidence while penalising only corroborated contradictions.

papers.title: Towards Fully-fledged GPU Multitasking via Proactive Memory Scheduling
papers.summary: Limited HBM capacity has become the primary bottleneck for hosting a growing number of increasingly larger-scale GPU tasks. While demand paging extends capacity via host DRAM, it can incur order-of-magnitude slowdowns due to the massive working sets of GPU workloads. However, we observe that GPU memory accesses are inherently predictable from kernel launch arguments, prior executions, and the asynchronous execution nature. Leveraging this opportunity, we propose MSched, an OS-level scheduler that extends GPU context switching to include proactive working set preparation. This approach coalesces fragmented, eventual, and expensive page faults into a single efficient migration. MSched combines parameterized templates with page fault feedback to accurately predict working sets, and co-designs the task scheduler and memory manager to resolve global access order and enforce near-optimal page replacement. Across scientific, deep learning, and LLM workloads, MSched outperforms demand paging by up to 186.69x and whole-process swapping by up to 8.63x. MSched is open-source and has been integrated into https://github.com/XpuOS/nvxsched.

papers.title: Online Graph Exploration under T-Interval Connectivity
papers.summary: We study deterministic exploration by a single agent in $T$-interval-connected graphs, a standard model of dynamic networks in which, for every time window of length $T$, the intersection of the graphs within the window is connected. The agent does not know the window size $T$, nor the number of nodes $n$ or edges $m$, and must visit all nodes of the graph. We consider two visibility models: in $KT_0$, the agent observes only its current node's identifier and port information; in $KT_1$, it additionally observes the identifiers of its currently available neighbors. We investigate two fundamental questions: the minimum window size that guarantees exploration, and the optimal exploration time under sufficiently large window size. For both models, we show that a window size $T = \Omega(m)$ is necessary, and we present deterministic algorithms whose required window size is $O(\xi(n,m)\cdot m + n \log^2 n)$, where $\xi(n,m) = \frac{\ln n}{1 + \ln m - \ln n}$. This window-size bound is tight for a wide range of $m$, in particular when $m = n^{1+\Theta(1)}$. Separately, for exploration time, we prove lower bounds of $\Omega((m - n + 1)n)$ in the $KT_0$ model and $\Omega(m)$ in the $KT_1$ model, even when the dynamic graph is $\infty$-interval-connected (i.e., even when all snapshots share a common spanning tree), and our algorithms match these time bounds up to a polylogarithmic factor. These bounds are also tight when parameterized solely by $n$: $\Theta(n^3)$ for $KT_0$ and $\Theta(n^2)$ for $KT_1$.

papers.title: Embedded Arena: Iterative Optimization via Hardware Feedback
papers.summary: As AI moves into the physical world, from robots to environmental sensors to medical wearables, it increasingly relies on local inference to meet latency, communication, or privacy constraints. Optimizing models for heterogeneous edge hardware such as microcontrollers (MCUs) requires simultaneously satisfying hard physical constraints on memory, power, and temperature while preserving accuracy, a multidimensional optimization that is today performed manually by experts. We ask whether an LLM agent can autonomously navigate this complex, multi-turn pipeline guided by real hardware feedback, and introduce a hardware-in-the-loop agent arena in which the agent iteratively refines both model and firmware by compiling, flashing, and measuring on real hardware, enabling closed-loop optimization. Frontier models, including Claude Opus 4.7 and Gemini 3.1 Pro, fail entirely without hardware feedback (0% deployment success), whereas our hardware-in-the-loop formulation achieves the first successful deployment within three iterations and can surpass human expert results within seven. This agentic co-optimization achieves 250x compression for vision models with <3.3% accuracy loss and 400x for audio with <6% Feature Error Rate loss, enabling battery-free operation on a commercial MCU via solar harvesting. We demonstrate practical impact in two real-world systems: an elk-detection camera trap (96.7% accuracy) and a phonetic-transcription wearable (8.37% FER) for child development research.

papers.title: BRAVR: An AP-Assisted Online DRL Mechanism for Interactive VR Bitrate Adaptation over Wi-Fi
papers.summary: Interactive virtual reality (VR) streaming over Wi-Fi requires stringent latency and reliability guarantees, which become increasingly difficult to achieve under dynamic channel conditions and shared-medium contention. These challenges make real-time bitrate adaptation a critical yet fundamentally difficult control problem, particularly under limited visibility of network conditions. This paper formulates VR bitrate adaptation as a network-aware, online decision-making problem and proposes BRAVR, a decentralized deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm that combines application-layer observations with lightweight wireless statistics collected at the Wi-Fi access point (AP) to balance visual quality, streaming performance, and multi-user airtime fairness. We implement BRAVR in a real VR streaming system and evaluate it on a physical Wi-Fi testbed against the VR-tailored NeSt-VR algorithm and an ablated BRAVR variant without AP telemetry. Experimental results show that, in the evaluated scenarios, BRAVR consistently achieves its design objectives, delivering robust quality of service (QoS) while avoiding sustained airtime overutilization. It also outperforms the AP-blind ablation, demonstrating the value of incorporating network-level information into the bitrate adaptation control loop. Overall, these results demonstrate the potential of AP-assisted online learning for decentralized interactive VR streaming over commodity Wi-Fi and provide practical insights into bitrate adaptation in shared wireless environments.

papers.title: ELDR: Expert-Locality-Aware Decode Routing for PD-Disaggregated MoE Serving
papers.summary: Equal load does not mean equal decode latency in prefill-decode (PD) disaggregated mixture-of-experts (MoE) serving. In bandwidth-bound decode, more distinct experts mean more weight loads and higher latency. We present ELDR, a lossless, expert-locality-aware decode router. Prefill signatures predict decode expert usage. Balanced $K$-means fits per-decoder centroids with background refitting. Locality-band routing selects the least-loaded worker among close matches. A block-granular cache keeps signatures exact under prefix caching. We evaluate ELDR in vLLM on up to 40 GPUs. Across three MoE models on 12 public task benchmarks and multilingual WildChat, it reduces median time-per-output-token (TPOT) by 5.4-14.5% on average across request rates and up to 17.8% over the best of four load-balancing baselines, preserving model outputs and token-to-expert assignments.

papers.title: Fuss-free cumulative universes: theory and practice
papers.summary: Universes are central to dependent type theory, and they are notoriously difficult to handle in a way that is both correct and usable. We propose a new "fuss-free" generalised algebraic presentation for polymorphic cumulative universes that dispenses with the intricate theory of coherent universe coercions in favour of a simpler formulation, which we prove equivalent by means of a normalisation theorem for the former. We study the fuss-free formulation by means of (1) an abstract specification of its bidirectional elaboration algorithm, and (2) a concrete implementation in Haskell. We also describe and implement an extension of the fuss-free universe hierarchy with a judgemental notion of datatype description from which prior notions of cumulative inductive type may be derived.

papers.title: A Physically-Realisable Quantum Programming Language with Quantum-Controlled Quantum Channels
papers.summary: In contrast to a classical bit, which can only take the value $0$ or $1$, its quantum counterpart---a qubit---can exist in a superposition of $0$ and $1$. This is a superposition of data values, and it is then tempting to superpose programs as well. Indeed, a particular superposition of programs, known as the quantum SWITCH, has attracted considerable attention. A natural way to superpose programs is conditional branching on quantum data, and several studies have pursued this idea. However, there is a well-known semantic difficulty with this approach, and the fundamental question of whether the languages proposed in prior work can be physically realised remains open. This paper proposes a physically realisable quantum programming language with quantum branching over quantum channels. We first analyse the semantic difficulty from an implementation perspective and show that the difficulty is caused by arbitrariness in the implementation. We then design a language that is free from this arbitrariness. As expected from its implementation-oriented design, our language is physically realisable. We argue for this from two directions: first, we give a method for compiling programs into quantum circuits; and second, we show that our programs stay within the physically admissible range, namely, that they neither yield probabilities greater than one nor violate causal inequalities. The absence of such violations is established through the inclusion of our language in QC-QC, a notion of realisability studied in physics.

papers.title: Greedy-Like Defective Coloring: Distributed Algorithms and Applications
papers.summary: A $d$-defective $c$-coloring of a graph $G=(V,E)$ is a coloring of the nodes $V$ with $c$ colors such that every node has at most $d$ neighbors of the same color. Distributed algorithms for computing different variants of defective coloring are at the core of most deterministic state-of-the-art distributed coloring algorithms, and they are also an important tool in many other distributed graph algorithms. In several cases, the overall complexity could be improved if some version of defective coloring could be solved more efficiently. Barenboim and Elkin [STOC '09] introduced a two-pass greedy algorithm that uses $p^2$ colors with defect $\lfloor \Delta/p\rfloor$ in $O(\Delta+\log^{\ast} n)$ rounds. This remains the best defect/color tradeoff for $O(\log^{\ast} n)$-time algorithms in bounded-degree graphs. This paper expands the capabilities of this two-pass algorithm. First, we generalize it to the \emph{list defective coloring} problem (Fuchs and Kuhn, [DISC '23]). Consequently, we obtain an alternative algorithm for computing a proper $(\Delta+1)$-coloring in $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{\Delta}) + O(\log^{\ast} n)$ rounds in the CONGEST model. Second, we analyze a generalized two-pass algorithm for standard defective colorings. We prove that if the number of colors $c$ is not a perfect square, we can improve the state-of-the-art defect for distributed $c$-colorings by a constant factor in most cases. However, we also prove a limitation: for any $c\geq 1$, this generalized algorithm cannot achieve a $c$-coloring with defect below $(1-o(1))\cdot\Delta/\sqrt{c}$.

papers.title: A Wavelength Borrowing Architecture for Optical Data Center Networks - Extended Version
papers.summary: The growth of east-west traffic, along with the cost and power consumption of electronic switching, is motivating the integration of a low-power, high-rate, all-optical layer within the data center network. This paper presents a spine-leaf all-optical architecture in which the default wavelength configuration, one wavelength per source--destination leaf pair, can be reconfigured to accommodate unbalanced traffic demand: wavelengths that are unused or lightly loaded at one leaf are borrowed by another leaf with higher demand. This topology-engineering capability is combined with a traffic-engineering scheme, based on two-hop detouring, enabling the control of wavelength load while limiting the amount of detoured traffic. A key feature of the architecture is that its degree of wavelength reconfigurability is set by a single tunable parameter, the borrowing degree $B$, ranging from none to full; performance evaluation shows that performance nearly equal to that of a fully reconfigurable architecture is achieved well below the maximum $B$, saving the complexity of a fully reconfigurable solutions. The optical fabric relies on mature, data-center-grade components, namely AWGs, AWGRs, colorless OXCs, and combiners. The reconfiguration speed and the adopted dynamic control policy make the architecture suitable for network tiers where the traffic varies on timescales of tens of minutes or more, e.g., among groups of racks (pods).

papers.title: Rendezvous under Variable Disorientation:The Algorithmic Power of Fixed Unit Distance
papers.summary: We study deterministic Rendezvous of two robots with lights under weak geometric and synchronization assumptions. Our focus is on Variable Disorientation (VD), where each robot may arbitrarily rotate, reflect, and rescale its local coordinate system at every \Look, and on VD+Fixed-Unit-Distance (FUD), where each robot's local unit distance remains fixed. We consider the one-sided visibility models FSTA and FCOM, and schedulers ranging from the energy-restricted RSYNCH and R-RSYNCH to fully asynchronous executions. Under VD, we prove color-independent impossibility results for FSTA under SSYNCH and for FCOM under ASYNCH, and establish sharp two-color boundaries under RSYNCH and R-RSYNCH. Under VD+FUD, we introduce periodic distance classes, which turn multipl icative changes of the physical distance into predictable cyclic phase shifts. This technique yields a two-color self-stabilizing non-$L$-Rendezvous algorithm for both FSTA and FCOM under RSYNCH and R-RSYNCH even with Non-Rigid movement. Under Rigid movement, periodic distance classes further yield an optimal three-color non-quasi-self-stabilizing algorithm for FSTA under SSYNCH, a four-color FSTA algorithm under $M$-atomic ASYNCH, and a four-color FCOM algorithm under CM-atomic ASYNCH. By guarding the latter phase mechanism with two additional colors and replacing its initial swap by passive initialization, we obtain a six-color FCOM algorithm under full ASYNCH, improving the previous twelve-color upper bound by a factor of two. These results show that a fixed local metric can serve as persistent cyclic memory, and clarify how metric stability, one-sided visibility, and scheduler atomicity jointly determine Rendezvous solvability and color complexity.

papers.title: PriorityFEC: Deadline-Aware Streaming FEC for KV-Cache Handoff in Edge Multi-Agent Systems
papers.summary: Collaborative edge large language model (LLM) systems often require repeated prefill computation when task contexts are transferred between agents. Reusing previously computed key--value (KV) caches can eliminate this overhead, but requires KV-cache delivery before the receiving agent begins decoding. Under strict deadlines and unreliable edge links, complete KV cache transfer may be infeasible, making the timely delivery of useful KV information critical. This paper proposes PriorityFEC, a utility-aware KV-cache handoff scheme that combines prioritized source transmission with adaptive loss recovery. PriorityFEC first organizes KV blocks into a utility-aware source queue to prioritize important information. It then employs ACK-sliding Streaming FEC and a lightweight Double Deep Q-Network (Double-DQN) scheduler to dynamically balance source delivery and repair transmission under deadline constraints. We implement PriorityFEC in a distributed edge LLM-serving prototype and evaluate it using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct across multiple workloads. Experimental results demonstrate that PriorityFEC preserves more useful KV information and achieves substantially higher task accuracy than competing transport schemes, particularly when the deadline is insufficient to deliver the complete KV cache.

papers.title: DIFFLET: A Fast Inference Engine for Diffusion Transformer Models on AWS Trainium
papers.summary: On AWS Trainium2, every component of a diffusion model runs as a program compiled ahead of time for fixed shapes, while pipelines differ across models, prompt lengths across requests, and caching decisions across denoising steps. We present Difflet, a serving engine in which five model pipelines share one compilation backend, joint attention is split across cores by attention head, and a host controller decides at each denoising step whether to run the denoiser or reuse its earlier output. A small probe program computes the caching signal on the device and returns one number per step, and a resident model process keeps every program loaded across requests. Across five image and video model families, fused attention accelerates denoiser steps by 1.2-4.3x over the same framework using PyTorch/XLA attention, and at 32.8k visual tokens it is the only attention that compiles. On four of the five models, resident serving is 1.5-3.4x faster than standalone runs that reload weights from a warm file cache for each generation.

papers.title: Decentralized Dynamic Stable Matching
papers.summary: We study decentralized computing of the player-optimal stable matching under unannounced player arrivals and departures. Without a common clock, arrival/departure events information, or direct communication, players can only make individual proposals to arms and observe individual accept/reject outcomes. We measure mismatch cost --- the number of rounds in which the realized matching differs from that round's POSM, as the time horizon $T$ grows. For known preferences, we develop a deterministic polynomial-time self-calibrating protocol with mismatch cost $O(t_*+K^2\log T)$, greatly improving the existing upper-bound $O(T^{1-1/K}(\log T)^{2/K})$. $K$ is the number of arms and $t_*$ the last event time in the problem instance. Each player runs the protocol using their own local time and proposal-outcome history, without knowing~$t_*$ or $T$. More generally, configuring our protocol with a non-decreasing polynomial-time-computable function $g(t)=\Omega(t)$ yields mismatch cost $O(g(t_*) + K^2 N_g(T))$, where $N_g(T)$ counts iterations of $t\mapsto t+g(t)$ below $T$. $g(t)$ reflects the protocol's convergence speed. The relationship between $g(t)$ and~$N_g(T)$ reflects the tradeoff between convergence speed and asymptotic mismatch cost. We show that any randomized protocol with convergence speed $g(t)\geq 1$ has worst-case expected cost $\Omega(t_* + N_g(T))$. Thus, up to a $K^2$ factor, our protocol with $g(t)=t$ is optimal among protocols with convergence speed $O(t_*)$. For unknown preferences on both sides, each player and arm observe their own sampled utilities after being matched. We develop a decentralized learning protocol with expected mismatch cost $O(t_*+K^4\Delta_{\mathrm{min}}^{-2}\log T)$, where $\Delta_{\min}$ measures the preference gaps. A complementary static-setting lower-bound adapted from the literature shows that dependencies on $T$ and $\Delta_{\min}$ are tight.

papers.title: Introducing Cluster Efficiency to LLM Serving: Pooling Economical Accelerators over Fast Interconnects
papers.summary: Long-context large language model (LLM) serving places substantial demands on compute, memory capacity, and memory bandwidth. Economical accelerators can offer these resources at lower cost, but their limited per-device capacity requires pooling across devices, making communication overhead critical. We study cluster efficiency, measured in tokens per dollar and per joule, and show how low-latency, high-bandwidth interconnects enable economical accelerators to retain their cost advantage. Guided by a characterization of coding-agent workloads and accelerator scaling, we realize this design on the Tenstorrent Galaxy, a cluster of Blackhole chips. The serving stack combines integrated communication engines, pipelined ring transfers, communication-computation overlap, and device-side decode replay to reduce collective overhead. Across three dense models in BF16 and 8-bit configurations with 8K-256K-token contexts, the Galaxy achieves 1.07-2.24$\times$ the tokens per dollar of an eight-GPU RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell server under a three-year acquisition-and-electricity cost model. Emulating TCP-class communication on the same chips reduces throughput by 23.5-67.4% and eliminates the cost advantage in every evaluated configuration. These results demonstrate how fast interconnects translate the per-dollar resource advantages of economical accelerators into cost-efficient long-context LLM serving.

papers.title: DMuon-2: Scaling Matrix Optimizers in Data Parallelism with Topology-Aware Matrix Ownership and Communication
papers.summary: Matrix optimizers such as Muon update whole weight matrices, which conflicts with the element- or row-wise sharding of data-parallel runtimes. Once parameters are sharded as well, matrix optimizers incur extra communication or repeated computation. We present DMuon, a matrix-granular optimizer runtime for PyTorch FSDP (ZeRO-2/3) and HSDP. DMuon assigns each matrix a unique owner, which performs the Newton--Schulz (NS) iteration and optimizer update on the full matrix, and balances the load across owners by computational cost. On HSDP, ownership is global across replicas, so the cluster keeps a single copy of gradients and optimizer state, and updated parameters are published across nodes as soon as they are ready, overlapping subsequent computation. This layout makes every collective sparse and variable in length, so DMuon schedules these collectives as their data becomes ready and routes them along the cluster's two-level network. On up to 256 H100 GPUs, across three dense LLMs and two VLA models, DMuon matches or exceeds the training throughput of PyTorch FSDP2 with AdamW, reaching 1.05$\times$ that of FSDP2 with AdamW at the median on 256 GPUs. The optimized parameter gathering and gradient reduction absorb the extra communication and computation a matrix optimizer requires. Against a gather-then-replicate Muon baseline, DMuon's throughput is 2.1 times as high at the median.

papers.title: The Program Logic of Abstract Interpretation
papers.summary: Hoare-style program logics and abstract interpretation are two of the principal frameworks for reasoning about programs, and their affinity has long been recognised informally: both derive over-approximate judgements about program behaviour by structural, syntax-directed reasoning. Turning this analogy into a formal correspondence runs into two challenges. First, the disjunction (or join) rule, sound and admissible in Hoare logic, becomes unsound over non-additive abstract semantics. Second, the extrapolation operators that make abstract interpretation effective on unbounded computations, i.e. widening and narrowing, have no analogue in the derivations of existing program logics. We introduce APPL (Abstract Program Property Logic), a Hoare-style program logic that provides a proof-theoretic foundation for abstract interpretation while addressing both challenges. The key technical idea is density: abstract semantics is additive over dense families of logical assertions. This leads to a density-guarded join rule that enables sound disjunctive reasoning over arbitrary abstract domains. We also internalise the application of widening and narrowing through inference rules for iterative commands. As a result, an entire analysis by abstract interpretation can be viewed as a logical derivation in APPL. The logic is sound over any abstract domain and, when the assertion language is expressive enough, it is also relatively complete. Finally, by interpreting nondeterminism through a monoidal operator, APPL provides a single logical framework that uniformly subsumes Hoare logic, incorrectness logic, and Hoare-style logics for hyperproperties, thereby enabling their abstraction. Remarkably, the density-guarded join rule introduced to handle non-additive abstract semantics is also fundamental in guaranteeing completeness for hyperproperties.

papers.title: Same Request, Different Answer: Quantization Amplifies Cache-Induced Divergence in LLM Serving
papers.summary: Major open-source serving stacks reuse the key-value tensors of a shared prefix by default. We measure what this prefix reuse costs in reproducibility. Holding model, decoding, seed and request order fixed at batch size one, we ran an eighty-episode multi-turn agentic tool-use workload with prefix reuse on and off across two engines and four weight formats. Without prefix reuse, repeated runs reproduced every token and log-probability in all ten configurations. With it, cache-hit and recompute paths diverged on both engines. On llama.cpp with GGUF weights this path divergence rises with quantization: for Qwen2.5-7B over ten independent server histories, it reached 37.4 percent of episodes at 16-bit and 82.5 percent at four-bit. Near-tie decisions became only about 1.2 times as common, while the cache-path change in top-two margins grew 4.9-fold from 16-bit to three-bit. Serving four-bit weights through 16-bit kernels left divergence not detectably different from 16-bit, placing the amplification mainly in the quantized execution path. At Q4_K_M, run-to-run divergence came mainly from llama.cpp's server-level prompt cache: under the canonical episode order it moved divergence by 37.5 points, and at its default, divergence spanned 20.0 to 28.7 percent under five random orders. With cache state restored, each path reproduced exactly while the two still differed. In the tested stacks, cached serving is irreproducible because the cache state is absent from the request and not reset by default. A single-turn bridge shows path divergence reaching task outcomes with no detectable net change in accuracy. We release the harness, logs, and analysis pipeline.

papers.title: AdaFloor: Adaptive Floor Planning and Rank-Time Reuse for Long-Tail MoE RL Rollouts
papers.summary: Synchronous MoE reinforcement-learning post-training suffers from response-length imbalance. Existing methods reduce request tails, yet completed ranks remain bound to Expert Parallelism (EP) collectives and expert ownership. In a representative 16-accelerator Qwen3-30B-A3B rollout, this dummy run traps 32.83% of rank-time. AdaFloor converts this EP-coupled capacity into bounded leases for auxiliary work to improve system resource efficiency through rank-time reuse. Historical prompt-tail prediction and a calibrated guard construct the KV-safe layout. AdaFloor then selects the floor-specific safe quorum schedule with the largest predicted release area. Its runtime shrinks the EP group and leases detached ranks until full-world restoration. Across three updated-policy seeds on DeepScaleR mathematical reasoning rollouts, its capacity-oriented Natural floor2 configuration with TailGuard reduces Vanilla's 29393.9 rank-seconds of dummy run by 96.15%. Rollout shortening eliminates 18693.6 rank-seconds, while coordinated exits convert another 9568.6 rank-seconds into reusable capacity, leaving 1131.7 rank-seconds. For sidecar reuse, its Planned residency floor4 configuration without TailGuard serves 3134 Qwen3-8B GSM8K queries per epoch at 99.46% accuracy and incurs only a 2 to 3% primary throughput reduction against the same configuration with sidecar execution disabled. Its latency-oriented Planned residency floor4 configuration with TailGuard reduces rollout time by 24.09% relative to Vanilla and by 2.31% relative to LengthSort with TailGuard. On public Eurus-2-RL code rollouts with the same model and 16-rank topology, AdaFloor reduces rollout time by 20.56% and dummy run by 89.13% while generated work and mean reward remain stable.
